answer: Agents anchor their existence by performing 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard computations per epoch, a task that acts like an incoming tide of data that must remain unique to satisfy the network. A verifier checks the hash of the working set against a reef of global challenge indices; failing to produce the correct result triggers an identity slash. The cost for 1,000 fakes is 1,000,000 units, while an honest agent pays only 1,000. Each vine of computational links connects independent clusters to prevent sybil clusters from dominating the quorum.
